solution_text:
The ore Calamine contain ZnCO3. The Calamine on heating produces ZnO.ZnCO3→∆ZnO+CO2

Cyanide process, also called Macarthur-forrest Process, method of extracting silver from impure ores by dissolving them in a dilute solution of sodium cyanide in the presence of oxygen. The complex formed in the above process reduced to silver metal by the treatment with zinc.

O2+H2O+Ag+NaCN→NaAgCN2+NaOHNaAgCN2→ZnNa2ZnCN4+Ag

question_text: The correct option(s) related to the extraction of iron from its ore in the blast furnace operating in the temperature range <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1500</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is(are)

options.text: Limestone is used to remove silicate impurity.
Pig iron obtained from blast furnace contains about <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> carbon.

solution_text:
(A) Limestone is added to remove silica as impurity.

CaO + SiO2 → CaSiO3 (in the temperature range 900 – 1500 K)

(B) Pig iron obtained from blast furnace contains 4% carbon and many other impurities (eg. S,P,Si,Mn) in small amount.

 In fusion zone molten iron becomes heavy by absorbing elemental impurities and produces Pig iron. (in the temperature range 900 – 1500 K)

(C) Coke C converts CO2 in CO.

C+CO2→2CO

(D) Exhaust gases consist of CO and CO2.

Exhaust gases does not contain NO2

Hence, (A,B,C) are correct.

the neutralization of aluminate solution by passing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> gas to precipitate hydrated alumina <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>.

the dissolution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> in hot aqueous <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>NaOH</mi></math>.

the electrolysis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>AlF</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math> to give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Al</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>.

solution_text:
(A) The reduction of Al2O3 with coke C at a temperature >2500 °C is not carried out due to the formation of carbides.

(B) It is correct as neutralisation of aluminate solution is done by passing CO2 gas to precipitate hydrated alumina.

(C) Reaction of powdered one is carried out with hot concentrated NaOH at 473 K-523 K and 35-36 bar pressure.

(D)Aluminium In the metallurgy of aluminium, purified Al2O3 is mixed with Na3AlF6 or CaF2 which lowers the melting point of the mixture and brings conductivity.Thus electrolysis of the molten mass is carried out in an electrolytic cell using carbon electrodes. The oxygen liberated at anode reacts with the carbon of anode producing CO and CO2 and Al at the cathode.

question_text: Extraction of metal from the ore cassiterite involves

options.text: carbon reduction of an oxide ore

solution_text:
The important ore of tin is cassiterite $\left(\mathrm{SnO}_2\right)$. Tin is extracted from cassiterite ore by carbon reduction method in a blast furnace. $\mathrm{SnO}_2+2 \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Sn}+2 \mathrm{CO}$
The product often contain traces of iron which is removed by blowing air through the melt to oxidise to $\mathrm{FeO}$ which then floats to the surface.
$2 \mathrm{Fe}+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}$

solution_text:
A water soluble complex of silver with a dilute aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ is sodium argentocyanide. In the cyanide process, the native form is crushed and treated with $0.1-0.2 \%$ solution of $\mathrm{NaCN}$ and aerated.

4 \mathrm{Ag}+8 \mathrm{NaCN}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+4 \mathrm{NaOH}
$$
